message.content:
Experiment: Conduct a preregistered, blocked, randomized repeated-run study on the 111-unit array. The **primary confirmatory comparison** will vary coupling at three pilot-selected levels while holding drive waveform, amplitude, frequency, disorder, geometry, and measurement protocol fixed. The three levels are intended to test an ordered dose response, but the primary estimand will be the prespecified high-versus-low coupling contrast; intermediate-versus-low and a linear trend across the three levels will be secondary contrasts.

Before the confirmatory study, run a separate, limited calibration pilot. Define the candidate coupling range from apparatus limits and select the lowest, middle, and highest settings that meet preregistered criteria for stable operation and distinct coarsening rates. Stable operation means no actuator saturation, no loss of array function, and no safety or apparatus limit violations. Coarsening separation will be assessed using the same spatial estimator planned for the main study, with pilot data used only to select settings and set measurement parameters, not included in confirmatory tests. Also use the pilot to assess synchronization, signal quality, reset effectiveness, run-to-run variability, feasible run throughput, and observation duration. Freeze settings, processing choices, and exclusions before collecting confirmatory data.

A run is one independently initialized trial at one assigned condition. Before each run, reset the array to a defined reference state using a documented procedure; verify the initial state against preregistered tolerances for measured displacement or shear. Randomize condition order within blocks, with each block containing one run at each coupling level. Use a documented washout/reset interval and verify that prespecified initial-state measures return to tolerance before the next run; otherwise repeat the reset before proceeding. If reset fails, label the trial a protocol failure before outcome analysis. Determine the minimum number of independent runs per condition from pilot variance and a preregistered precision target for the high-versus-low onset-time contrast. Fix this number before the confirmatory study, set a maximum feasible number in advance, and do not stop early based on observed effects. Report the number of runs, failures, and exclusions by condition.

Record actuator command and delivered motion, spatial images, and unit-level motion or shear with a shared clock and drive-phase reference. Define protocol tolerances for delivered amplitude, frequency, and phase error during the pilot, then freeze them before the main study. Measure disorder using a prespecified array-level measure and verify that it remains within its preregistered tolerance across coupling conditions. Trials outside these tolerances are flagged before outcome analysis; report them and the reasons for exclusion, and conduct a sensitivity analysis including flagged trials when measurements permit. A coupling effect will be interpreted as the causal effect of the coupling intervention. It will not be attributed specifically to coarsening if coupling also changes drive delivery, disorder, or another measured physical property.

For each run, estimate the spatial correlation function using the same prespecified unit-pair or image-based estimator, spatial domain, and temporal windows. Fit the prespecified model over a fixed distance range to obtain correlation length and uncertainty. Choose the estimator, fit model, and distance range during calibration, then preregister them; also preregister a small set of alternative fit ranges for sensitivity analysis. Estimate coarsening rate from the prespecified slope of correlation length over time before temporal-order onset, or over the full fixed observation interval for runs without detected onset.

Measure temporal order from synchronized unit-level signals in sliding windows defined in drive cycles. Apply the preregistered preprocessing steps, including detrending and tapering, and calculate subharmonic power at half the drive frequency relative to the median power in fixed neighboring-frequency bands that exclude the subharmonic and drive peaks. Select window length and step during calibration so the subharmonic can be resolved at the actual drive frequency; fix them in drive cycles before the main study. The observation interval will be fixed in drive cycles based on calibration and apparatus limits, and will be identical across conditions.

Calibrate the detection threshold before the confirmatory study using null signals that preserve relevant features of non-crystalline measurements. Use surrogate signals generated by phase or block randomization within runs, with the method and number of surrogates fixed in the protocol; verify that the surrogates preserve the measured spectrum and short-timescale structure while disrupting persistent subharmonic phase locking. Set the threshold to control the run-level false-positive probability at a preregistered level across the full search over windows. Define a qualifying onset as the first window in which the normalized subharmonic measure exceeds that threshold for a preregistered number of consecutive windows, with the persistence requirement stated in drive cycles. Runs without qualifying onset by the fixed observation limit are right-censored. Define persistence as the time from onset until the measure falls below threshold for the preregistered number of consecutive windows, or until the observation limit. Report phase stability as a secondary outcome. Missing or corrupted windows will be handled using preregistered rules; do not interpolate them for onset detection.

The primary outcome is onset time in drive cycles. The primary estimand is the difference in restricted mean onset time through the fixed observation limit between high and low coupling, with later or undetected onset represented by censoring. Estimate it using a survival model with coupling condition as a fixed effect and block or experimental day as a stratification or random effect. Estimate persistence using a prespecified censored time-to-loss model. Analyze repeated spatial and spectral measurements with hierarchical models including run-level and block/day effects; runs, not windows or time samples, are the independent units. Report effect estimates and uncertainty intervals. Test the secondary dose-response trend and whether pre-onset correlation length or coarsening rate predicts onset across conditions. Treat mediation through correlation length as conditional mechanistic evidence, not proof of a unique causal pathway. Compare the preregistered temporal alternatives by testing whether changes in coarsening precede and predict onset, whether both observables change with drive, and whether temporal order predicts subsequent coarsening.

After completing the primary coupling study, conduct a **staged drive-only control** as a separate comparison: hold coupling and disorder at the middle primary-study settings and test low, reference, and high drive levels selected and frozen during calibration within the stable operating range. Analyze each drive contrast against the reference condition; this is not a factorial coupling-by-drive test, so do not infer a coupling-by-drive interaction. Treat this control as confirmatory only if its settings, sample-size target, and analysis are preregistered before its data collection; otherwise label it exploratory. A separately varied disorder condition remains optional and exploratory unless similarly specified and preregistered.

Rationale: The target paper reports that wave coarsening drives time crystallization. The supplied aggregate export is consistent with increasing correlation width and an early rise followed by relatively stable mean shear, but it contains neither synchronized raw signals for measuring temporal order nor run-level replication for estimating causal effects. Its 2,199 time samples are not independent runs, and the aggregation underlying the exported width standard errors is unspecified. The export therefore motivates the measurements but cannot validate temporal precedence or causation.

The revised protocol makes the primary causal contrast explicit: randomized coupling levels with drive and disorder held fixed, using independently initialized runs and a prespecified high-versus-low onset-time estimand. Pilot calibration establishes feasible settings and measurement parameters without using pilot outcomes as confirmatory evidence. Fixed signal-processing rules, run-level null calibration, a family-wise onset criterion, and explicit handling of censoring and failed trials reduce analytic discretion. The staged drive control tests a plausible parallel-response explanation while avoiding unsupported claims about a factorial interaction. If coupling alters additional physical properties, results support the effect of the intervention as implemented, not a claim that coarsening alone caused temporal order. Conclusions remain specific to this array and tested parameter range.
